Name: Sri Basaveshwara Temple
Description: The temple comprises a garbhagraha, antarala and sabhamandapa. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga. The doorframe of the garbhagraha is of panchasakha order. The interior of the sabhamandapa has four free standing pillars. The ceiling is decorated with Asta-Dikpalas and Nataraja in the central comportment. The door frame of the sabhamandapa is Panchasakha on its either side are dvarapala sculptures. The temple has three entrances. The exterior of the Kaksasana is decorated with Kalasa. Opposite to the temple is Nandimandapa. The temple has three inscriptions of 11-12 century A. D.

Name: Basavanna Well
Description: Basavanna well is in Bagewadi city of Bagewadi taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Eshwara Temple
Description: This temple consists of a garbhagrha, an antarala, a sabhamandapa and a mahamandapa. A Sivalinga is enshrined in the garbhagraha. At the base of the antarala door are chauri bearers. In the sabhamandapa are four free standing pillars. The sabhamandapa has entrances on the north and east. Adjoining the east entrance is a Mahamandapa. It contains six free standing huge pillars and sixteen corresponding pilastars. In the Mahamandapa are Kaksasanas, which have carvings of nagara form and a sikhara on the exterior. The exterior walls of the sabhamandapa have panjara kosthas. The adhistthana of the sabhamandapa has upana, jagati, gala, vedike. The adhisthana of the garbhagraha consists of upan, jagati, tripat takumduda and vedi.

Name: Narayanadeva temple
Description: The temple consists of a garbhagraha, an antarala and an open mukhamandapa. The doorframe of the garbhagraha is tri-shakha. The lalatabimba contains a tity Gajalakshmi bimba. Inside the sabhamandapa are two free standing pillars? On either side of the doorway are Kalasa motifs. The kadamabanagara or phamsana superstructure is damaged. It seems to be a Rashtrakuta temple.

Name: Siddeshwara Temple
Description: This north-east facing cave temple has a small doorway to enter the hall. A flight of steps leads to the garbhagraha. In the garbhagraha is a sculpture of Revanasiddhesvara. The garbhagraha is 15 feet below the land level.

Name: Sri Rameshwara temple
Description: This is a trikuta temple. It comprises three garbhagrahas each with an antaralas, a common sabhamandapa and a mukhamandapa. Each garbhgraha enshrined a Sivalinga. On either side of the east facing garbhagrha door is a Saiva dvarapala. In the sabhamandapa are four free standing pillars, and four empty Kosthas. In the mukhamandapa are four free standing pillars, and Kaksasanas.This temple is in good condition.

Name: Sri Sangameshwara Temple
Description: Sri Sangameshwara temple  is in Kadakola village  of Bagewadi taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Ramalingeshwara temple
Description: The temple consists of a garbhagraha and sabha mandapa. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga. The doorframe of the garbhagraha has a single shakha. There is a pradaksginapatha around the garbhagraha. The interior of the sabhamandapa has four freestanding pillars. In the centre of the sabhamandapa is seated Nandi. There is no Sikhara over the garbhagraha.

Name: Lakshminarasimha temple
Description: This dvikuta temple comprises two garbhagraha, antarala and a mukhamandapa. The garbhagrahas have trisakha door frames. The lalatabimas of the two garbhagrahas have tiny Gajalakshmi bimba. There is a Kakshasana around the mukhamandapa. There is an inscription connected with this temple dated 1189 A.D. It states that the temple was built by Chowdisetti, grandfather of an officer called  Shankara Swami.

Name: MuktheshwaraLakshminarayana and Kashivishwanatha temple
Description: This temple consists of a navaranga an antarala and a garbhagraha. The pillars at the centre of the navaranga are decorated. There are two pillars at the entrance to the antarala. Above these pillars is a makaratorana panel. The garbhagraha enshrined  a linga.

Name: Sri Ramalinga temple
Description: The temple consists of a garbhagraha, antarala and an open Mukhamandapa. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga. There are four freestanding pillars in the sabhamandapa. The Mukhamandapa has three entrances. There is a Kakshasana around the Mukhamandapa. On stylistic grounds the temple belong to 12th century A.D.

Name: Shankarlingadeva temple
Description: This east-facing temple comprises a garbhagraha, antarala sabhamandapa and a modern mukha mandapa. In the grabhagraha is a Sivalings. The ceiling has a plain relief of Padma. The doorframe of the garbhagraha is trisakha. In the lalatabimba of the door frame of the garbhagraha is a tiny Ganesha motif. The antarala ceiling has a plain relief of Padma. The sabhamandapa has four freestanding pillars. There are eight devakosthas in the sabhamandapa. The renovated mukhamandapa stands on a high platform. The temple may have been built in the 13th centuryA. D.

Name: Shankarlingadeva temple Dhulked
Description: Shankarlingadeva temple is in Dhulked village of Indi taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Revanasiddeshwara temple
Description:
This temple consists of a gabhagraha, an antarala, a sabhmanadapa and a mukhamandapa. In the garbhagraha is an icon of Ganesha on the pitha. Originally there is a Sivalinga on it.  On either side of the antarala are Jalandharas. In the sabhmandapa are four freestanding pillars. The sabhmandapa doorframe is simple.  In front of the Mukhamandapa are inscription set up. There is also a bali pitha near by the inscriptions. Further in frornt of balipitha is a Makaratorana an attractive architectural part of the temple. Within the Prakara of the temple are many small shrines. It appears the temple was originally built in bricks.
This temple consists of garbhagraha and a sabhamandapa. A sivalinga is enshrined in the garbhagraha. In the sabhamandapa are four freestanding pillars. A Nandi image is at the centre of the sabhamanadpa. Inside the temple is a mutilated Durga sculpture. Outside the temple is an image of surya installed on a Visnu Pitha.

Name: Sri Durga devi temple
Description: This temple consists of a garbhagraha, an antarala, a sabhmandapa and a mukhamandapa. A Durga idol is enshrined in the garbhagraha. Over the garbhagraha is a Sikhara. It contains many bas-reliefs of Chamundi in different postures. In front of the temple is a Simhamandapa. A loose is culture is in the Mandapa. The temple has a prakara wall.

Name: Sangameshwara temple
Description: This is a trikuta temple. It comprises three garbhagrhas, an antarala and a sabhmandapa. Each garbhagraha houses a Sivalinga. In the sabhmandapa are four free standing pillars? The doorframe consists of three shaklhas of usual order. Inside the sabhamandapa are four devakosthas. In the sabhamandapa is an ornate Nandi. On the southern side of the percept that surrounds the temple is a big gateway and on the northern sides are steps leading the river Bhima, inside it are an open roofed Verandha supported by many pillars. To the north –east of the temple is a small shrine facing south and on the western wall exterior are slabs of two Viragals of usual type and a Naga sculpture. Over the garbhagraha is superstructure of later period, stylistically it is of C.12-13th century A.D.

Name: Eshwara temple Nandaragi
Description: Eshwara temple  is in Nandaragi village of Indi taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Maruthi temple
Description: This modern temple has a garbhagraha and mandapa. The garbhagraha contains a Maruti sculpture of later date. The large courtyard has many mandapas.

Name: Shivayogeshwara temple
Description: The temple is in Indo-Islamic style. It consists of a garbhagraha and a mukhamandapa of later period. Originally the temple was a mosque. Later it was converted into a Siva temple by installing a Nandi in front of the garbhagraha. All the four corners of the Kapota portion has Nandi image. The garbhagraha walls have arch model projections. The superstructure of the temple is of dome type. On stylistic ground this temple resembles Islamic style. It has a prakara wall. Inside the prakara wall are many small rooms, which have arched facade.

Name: Shiva temple
Description: This is a trikuta temple. It comprises three garbhagrhas, each with an antaralas and a common sabhamandapa. The north facing garbhagrha enshrined a Sivalinga. Its doorframe is well decorated. On either side of it are saiva dvarapalas. The east and west facing garbhagrahas have Pitha without Linga. The doorframes of these garbhagrahas resemble the door frame of the north garbhagraha. In the sabhamandapa are four free standing pillars. In the mukhamandapa are two free standing pillars. The temple stands on an adhisthana. The exterior wall of the temple is decorated.

Name: Bhageshwara temple
Description: This temple consists of a garbhagrAha, an antarala and a sabhamandapa. A Sivalinga is enshrined in the garbhagraha. The garbhagraha door frame has decorated sakhas. On either side of the antarala wall are jalandhras. In the sabhamandapa are four free standing pillars? Its walls are renovated. Over the garbhagraha is a superstructure of later date.

Name: Basavanna temple
Description: This temple consists of two garbhagraha an open antarala and a sabhamandapa. There is an open antarala in front of the east facing garbhagraha. The east facing garbhagraha has a Sivalinga. The navaranga has entrances on the north and the south. Both the garbhagrahs have sikharas.

Name: Shiva temple Nalatwad
Description: Shiva temple is in Nalatwad village of Muddebihal taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Veerabhadra temple
Description: This temple consists of a garbhagraha an anatarala and a sabhamandapa. Anjaneya idol is enshrined in the garbhagraha.

Name: Maruthi temple tumbgi
Description: Maruti temple is in Tumbgi village of Vmuddebihal taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Ramalingeshwara temple Chandkavathe
Description: The temple consists of a garbhagraha antarala and sabhamandapa. This temple is in most dilapidated condition. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga. The sabhamandapa has fallen. The exterior walls of the temple are decorated with richly carved sculptures. The Kadambanagara or phamsana Sikhara has fallen.

Name: Haggappaya temple
Description: The temple faces east. It has two vertical moldings at each front corner and three at each rear corner. The doorframe is plain. On either side of the doorway are dvarapalas. The front of the threshold has a carved relief of standing couple with folded hands. Over the garbhagraha is a modern Sikhara. In front of the shrince is a low plinth.

Name: Madivaleshwara temple
Description: The temple consists of a garbhagraha and two mukhamamdapas, each with their arched façade, of Ashlar Masonry. The garbhagraha contains a face of the saint madivala. It is decorated with braze and silver. The front mukhamandapa is built perhaps by another devote sometime after the construction of the original structure containing a shrine and a mukhamandapa with arched façade. Otherwise, the three-arched façade for the inner mukhamandapa is superfluous. This madivalappa, the local people say, is the name celebrated madivalada machiah, one of the famous Shivasharanas of the 12th C.  A.D. And this is his birth  place.

Name: Mallaya temple
Description: The temple faces north. It consists of a square hall with exactly similar rectangular side halls on each side and an octagonal shrine, on the southern side of it. Each side hall on the east, north and west has entrances. The doorframe on each side is plain. On either side of the doorway are dvarapalas. The lalatabimba contains a tiny Ganesha bimba. In front of the northern door is a small parapet with three openings each on one side for entrance. 4713151, 0798875

Name: Mallikarjuna temple
Description: The temple faces west. It comprises a garbhagraha, antarala, sabhamandapa and mukhamandapa. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga. There are four freestanding pillars in the sabhamandapa. A Nandi of later date kept in the centre. The doorframe of the sabhamandapa consists of panchasakhars.  In the sabhamandapa is an inscription. The mukhamandapa has a kaksasana. The exterior walls are plain. Over the garbhagraha is renovated sikhara.

Name: Someshwara temple
Description: This east facing temple consists of a garbhagraha, antarala, sabhamandapa and mukhamandapa. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga, locally called Somanatha. The doorframe of the garbhagraha is panchashakha. The sculpture of the Lalatabimba is unidentified. The antarala has tri-shakha doorframe. The ceiling is decorated with a Padma motif. There are four freestanding pillars in the sabhamandapa. Inside the sabhamandapa are six devakosthas. The mukhamandapa has fallen. The original doorframe is replaced by wooden doors. The Kakshasana of the Mukhamanda has fallen. The exterior plain walls have bhadra - salilantara. On the exterior walls of the garbhagraha are three devakosthas, the western and the southern being in a dilapidated condition.

Name: Kallalingeshwara temple
Description: This Dvikuta temple faces east. It consists of two garbhagrahas, antarala, a common sabhamandapa and a mukhamandapa. In the garbhagraha is a Sivalinga. The doorframe of the garbhagraha is trisakha over the doorframe is sculpture of dancing Nataraja. There are four freestanding pillars in the sabhamandapa. The interior walls of the sabhamandapa have two empty devakosthas. In the centre of the sabhamandapa is a seated Nandi. The lalatabimba contains a tiny Ganesha Sculpture.

Name: Chabuk savarana darga
Description: Chabuk savarana darga is in Vijayapura city of Vijayapura taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Hanumantha temple
Description: Hanumantha temple is in Torvi village of Vijayapura taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Bali hanumantha temple
Description: In the out skirts of the village is a Hanuman temple of later date, locally called Bailu Hanumantanagudi. It is said that this Hanuman idol was brought from the village Bairige and installed in this temple. On either side of the Hanuman idol the sculptures of Linga and Ganesha was installed by the village elder Hariyappa Brahmana.

Name: Maleswamy temple
Description: Maleswamy temple is in Bellehubbi village of Vijayapura taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Malikarjuna temple
Description: This temple consists of a garbhagraha an antarala and a navaranga. There is a Linga in the garbhagraha. On the north and east side of the navaranga are small garbrhagrahas. The temple has an entrance on the south. Some noteworthy sculptures of this temple is Ganapati, Mahishamardini, Vishnu, Sarasvati, Surya, Saptamatrike panel and Naga sculpture.

Name: Sideshwara temple
Description: The temple consists of a garbhagrabha and mukhamandapa. The lalatabimba of the garbhagraha doorframe contains a tiny Virabhadra motif. The pillars of the mukhamandapa are decorated with richly carved sculptures. The temple has large prakara. It seems the temple was built in 1780 A. D.

Name: Mahipatieswamy temple
Description: The garbhagraha enshrined a Sivalinga on a pitha. Over the Sivalinga is a five-hooded serpent of Panchaloha. The garbhagraha has a pradaksinapatha.

Name: Mallikarjuna temple Kakhandaki
Description: The garbhagraha enshrined a Sivalinga on a pitha. Over the Sivalinga is a five-hooded serpent of Panchaloha. The garbhagraha has a pradaksinapatha.

Name: Sangameshwara temple Kakhandaki
Description: Only the garbhagrha has remained. It enshrined a Sivalinga on a pitha. Over the Sivalinga is a seven-hooded serpent of brass.

Name: Veerabhadra temple Kakhandaki
Description: Veerabhadra temple is  in Kakhandaki village of Vijayapura taluk in Vijayapura district.

Name: Tajbavadi
Description: Tajbavadi is in Vijayapura city of Vijayapura taluk in Vijayapura district.
